explain.1: Load PyTorch, so we can use torch.something.
explain.2: Load PyTorch's ready-made functions (softmax, cross_entropy) under the short name F.
explain.4: Our training text: the only thing your model will learn from.
explain.5: set() keeps each character once. sorted() puts them in order. This is the vocabulary.
explain.6: len() counts the characters in the vocabulary.
explain.7: An empty dictionary. It will hold pairs like 'h' → 3.
explain.8: Another empty dictionary, for the reverse: 3 → 'h'.
explain.9: enumerate() gives each character with its position: 0 and the 1st character, 1 and the 2nd, and so on.
explain.10: Save this pair in the dictionary: character → number.
explain.14: An empty list. It will hold every example's last 8 letters.
explain.15: An empty list for every 'next character' (the right answers).
explain.16: Go through the text, stopping 8 letters before the end, so every example has a next letter.
explain.17: Take the 8 letters starting at i, turn each into its number, and add that row of 8 numbers.
explain.18: The letter right after those 8: the answer for this example.
explain.19: Turn the list into a tensor: a table with one row of 8 numbers per example.
explain.21: Show how many examples we have: 44 windows of 3 letters, each with the letter that comes next.
explain.24: Fix the random numbers, so you get the same start as the page.
explain.25: The embedding table: 3 small random numbers for each of the 14 letters. requires_grad_() lets PyTorch find their pushes.
explain.26: 3 small random position numbers for each of the 8 places.
explain.27: The query weights: turn the last letter's 3 numbers into its question.
explain.28: The key weights: turn each letter's 3 numbers into its label.
explain.29: The value weights: turn each letter's 3 numbers into what it offers.
explain.30: The output weights: turn the final 3 numbers into 14 scores, one per next letter.
explain.31: Keep all the model's numbers in one list, so we can move them all together.
explain.32: Count every number in the model: 42 + 24 + 9 + 9 + 9 + 42.
explain.35: Define the model's guess. It runs only when we call it, for one or many windows at once.
explain.36: Each letter's numbers: its embedding plus its place's position numbers.
explain.37: The last letter's question: its numbers × the query weights.
explain.38: Every letter's label: its numbers × the key weights.
explain.39: What every letter offers: its numbers × the value weights.
explain.40: Each label · the question (a dot product), ÷ 1.73. One match per letter.
explain.41: Turn the 8 matches into shares that add up to 1: the attention.
explain.42: Each value × its share, added up: the mix.
explain.43: Add the last letter's own numbers, × the output weights: 14 scores. Also give back the attention.
explain.46: How big each move is. 0.5 works well for these numbers.
explain.47: Train 300 times: predict, measure, find directions, move.
explain.48: Guess for all 39 examples at once.
explain.49: b) Measure, all in one call: for every example, softmax its scores into chances, take the right answer's chance, −log it, then average them all. One number: how wrong. Smaller is better.
explain.50: Go through each of the model's tables.
explain.51: Forget the old pushes before finding new ones.
explain.52: c) Find directions: PyTorch works out every score's gradient (chance − goal, averaged over the examples) and puts them in .grad.
explain.53: Go through each of the model's tables.
explain.54: Move every number a little against its push.
explain.55: % is the remainder. This is true at steps 0, 50, 100, … so we print every 50 steps.
explain.56: Show the step number and the loss.
explain.57: Show the loss after the last step.
explain.60: Fix the random numbers, so you get the same result every time.
explain.61: Start the new text with 8 letters, so the model has a full window.
explain.62: Write 40 more characters, one per round.
explain.63: The last 8 letters written so far, as numbers: a window of one example.
explain.64: Guess the next letter for this one window.
explain.66: Spin the weighted wheel and take out the picked number.
explain.67: Add the picked letter to the text.
